thread:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for release v1.5.0 -> 10% traffic in eu-west. (id: rl-2026-05-20-042)

maya: seeing a P95 latency jump in eu-west since 04:10 UTC. p50 ~120ms (was 30ms), p95 ~900ms (was 300ms). errors steady otherwise. :thinking_face:

omar: @maya can you paste the percentiles over last 10m?

maya: 10m window: p50 120ms, p90 460ms, p95 900ms, p99 1.2s. qps same. slow tail only in eu-west canary nodes.

kevin: :eyes: request to pause canary?

gloria: we should hold at 10% until we know root cause. requesting a Stop/hold.

deploy-bot: Received hold request. Current rollout state: HOLD requested by gloria at 04:12 UTC. Suggested commands: `redwood rollout hold --id rl-2026-05-20-042 --region eu-west` or `redwood traffic shift --id rl-2026-05-20-042 --to 0`

omar: +1 hold. can we pin back to stable (v1.4.9) for eu-west while we investigate?

kevin: pin would be safest. command to pin: ```
redwood deploy pin --region eu-west --service llm-inference --version v1.4.9
```

maya: agree. quick checklist before pin: confirm warm caches + KV cache compatibility. I think v1.4.9 uses same cache format but will run a quick smoke.

sre-bot: Alert: node eu-west-canary-3 reported high tail latency and elevated GPU memory contended logs at 04:09 UTC. Logs: `/var/log/inference/worker.log` snippet attached.

gloria: I'm owner for this rollout. approving pin to v1.4.9 and rollback if smoke fails. @kevin can you execute?

kevin: executing pin now. will throttle shifts to avoid cold starts. running: `redwood deploy pin ...` (started 04:16 UTC)

deploy-bot: Action: PIN applied -> v1.4.9 in eu-west. Traffic held at 10% to avoid user impact. Pin command returned success (ops-id: pin-8812).

maya: running smoke tests on pinned version: small sample requests returning in ~35-40ms. KV cache warmup looks OK.

omar: recommend full rollback to 0% and then progressive roll forward after fixes. We should also mark the release as rolled back in release notes.

gloria: agreed. schedule rollback to 0% for canary and cutover stabilization window. I'll open a rollback ticket and update the change window.

kevin: executing traffic shift to 0% (gentle) -> started 04:28 UTC. will monitor for 10m.

deploy-bot: Traffic shift in progress -> canary eu-west -> 0% (gradual). ETA 6m.

maya: monitoring metrics. p95 dropped back toward baseline as traffic shifted. initial signs look good.

gloria: created ticket INF-3247 Rollback v1.5.0 canary eu-west -> 0%. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3247. adding owners: gloria, maya, kevin.

omar: annotate release notes: https://redwood.dev/releases/v1.5.0 - pls add note: "Canary paused and rolled back in eu-west due to increased tail latency; investigating kernel scheduling behaviour on canary nodes."

kevin: added note and pinned a short changelog and rollback entry.

gloria: I'll coordinate postmortem. keep the rollout blocked until ENG-POSTMORTEM complete and we have a mitigation (hotfix or config).

deploy-bot: Hold enforced on rl-2026-05-20-042. Rollback ticket INF-3247 created. Ops runbook step: if hotfix ready -> create new canary with 2% starting traffic in eu-west and monitor p95 < 350ms for 30m.

maria: (from infra) adding: we saw a microburst GC + NVidia driver swap on canary-3 at 04:08 UTC. collecting full node dump.

maya: thanks @maria. once dumps are in, let's correlate to request queue spikes.

kevin: closing loop: rollback to stable complete at 04:34 UTC. traffic eu-west canary = 0%. All monitoring dashboards green for stable traffic.

gloria: thanks team. next steps: 1) triage INF-3247 2) decide on retry strategy/canary parameters (start 2% -> 5% -> 10% with 30m observation) 3) don't schedule wide cutover until signoff.

omar: noted. I'll prep a short blameless postmortem template and share in #postmortems.

deploy-bot: Thread closed by deploy-bot: rollout halted and rolled back to stable in eu-west. For follow-ups, reference INF-3247.

kevin: :thumbsup: thanks everyone.

maya: filing a short incident note for weekly sync.

gloria: assigning follow-ups and will ping owners tomorrow 09:30 UTC. :calendar:
